navigation.check: All four stages can be opened and stage labels remain Plan, Simulate, Analyze, Review.
Every one of the 13 tools can be selected from its stage flyout.
Unavailable tools remain discoverable, expose a reason, and cannot activate.
A different-stage click retains the existing first-available-tool behavior.
Drawer always shows current stage and tool name, including direct/programmatic destinations.
All sibling names and success/warning/count state are visible in the flyout without horizontal scrolling.
Map Inspector replaces tool content as before and Back returns to prior tool.

keyboardAndPointer.check: Tab reaches all stage triggers and available tool choices in a logical order.
Up/Down and Home/End follow the documented flyout model.
Enter/Space opens a stage chooser and selects a tool.
Escape closes the flyout and restores focus to the stage trigger.
Closing the drawer returns focus to a mounted stage control, not a removed tool-tab button.
Tool selection announces/lands on the active tool heading without trapping focus.
Pointer click opens and selects; hover is not required; dismissal does not swallow a map or drawer click.
Tap opens stage tools and tap selects a named tool; no hover behavior is required.

directNavigation.check: Open current RF result reaches Results/RF without an extra flyout click.
Open vertical path profile reaches Propagation's advanced path-profile section directly.
Run History source actions inspect or regenerate the chosen Run directly.
Report source and generated-report navigation preserve Scenario/Version/Run context.
Validation/attention action opens its exact target directly.

lazyLoading.check: Opening a stage flyout does not load Propagation or RF Diagnostics research chunks; selecting the existing feature triggers its current lazy boundary.
Core Lab chunk remains unloaded until 5G Core is selected.
Report chunk remains unloaded until Report is selected.
Run History chunk remains unloaded until Run history is selected.
Experiments chunk remains unloaded until Experiments is selected.
Compare build chunks before/after 8B; no lazy feature is folded into the eager shell.

responsive.check: Rail, drawer, flyout, command bar, map, toolbar, and legend fit with map dimensions unchanged.
Grouped command bar stays readable; no widening of drawer.
Flyout overlays without pushing map; workspace/RF/result state remain visible.
Touch-sized flyout works with vertical rail and usable map.
Bottom stage bar and tool sheet work; no horizontal overflow; action and map inspection remain usable.
Assert document scrollWidth equals viewport width and all tool names remain discoverable.

lineageAndResults.check: User can answer Project, Scenario, Version/no-Version, and draft state without a deep panel.
CURRENT, STALE, HISTORICAL, UNAVAILABLE, and UNSUPPORTED remain explicit when applicable.
A short source Run stays discoverable globally; full run identity remains in Results/Run History.
Optimization/overlap/serviceability/RF metrics remain discoverable in Results and relevant legend after moving out of global header.
Browser-local draft autosave and immutable Version save remain distinct in labels and Project menu.
Results RF, Optimization, Interference, Compare, and Candidates views remain intact.

invariance.check: Compare RF request payloads for the same plan before/after navigation changes; navigation itself issues no RF request.
Optimization request and input fingerprints remain identical for unchanged inputs.
Project/Scenario, Run source, historical result, and Report semantics are unchanged.
Planning/Advanced/Research capability state and scientific terminology are retained.
Opening menus introduces no API calls or feature imports; selecting tool follows its existing boundary.

executionOrder: Unit/component tests for flyout and focus
Responsive screenshots at all five widths
outOfScope: RF/optimizer behavior tests unrelated to invariance
